New Temporary & Permanent Course Email
The New Temporary & Permanent Course Email is distributed to all faculty, deans, and associate and assistant deans on the last weekday of each month. Recipients then have seven days to submit comments to the CASC Chair, GEC Chair, or Dean of the Graduate School regarding any potential or perceived content overlap involving a new temporary or permanent course.
The email serves two purposes:
Provides notice of upcoming Faculty Senate review. Courses included in the email have already been reviewed and approved by their respective College Curriculum Committees and will next be reviewed by the appropriate Faculty Senate Curriculum Committee: CASC, GEC, or Graduate Council.
Provides an opportunity to identify potential content overlap. College Curriculum Committees may review the courses included in the email to identify any potential or perceived overlap with courses offered or proposed by other colleges. Any concerns can then be raised before the courses proceed to Faculty Senate Curriculum Committee review.

Credential Type
Tags: programs
Short Description: Identifies the type of academic credential awarded for a program. (Degree, Major, Minor, Certificate)
Credential Type

The degree is the academic credential awarded by the University upon successful completion of an approved program of study and its associated requirements. Degrees may include bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees.
The major is the primary field of study within a degree program, consisting of a defined set of courses and requirements that students must complete.
University Manual 8.20.40 Major Fields of Study. An undergraduate student’s concentrated field of study in a degree-granting college shall be the student’s “major”; Fannon Institute students may have a “preferred major.” The major field of study for graduate students shall be the student’s “program.”

Undergraduate programs are required to have a minimum or 120 credits, and a maximum of 148 (UM 8.21.10)
Undergraduate programs shall include at least 6 credits of free electives (UM 8.21.10)
General Education requirements shall apply to all undergraduate programs (UM 8.21.11)
A cumulative average of at least 2.00 is required to graduate from all undergraduate degrees. (UM 8.22.10)
Master’s degree programs with thesis require a minimum of 30 credits. 18 must be from content-based courses, 6 must be thesis courses. (GSM 7.44.1)
Master’s degree programs without thesis require a minimum of 30 credits. (GSM 7.45.1)
Doctoral students must complete a Program of Study with a minimum of 64 credit hours beyond the undergraduate degree (GSM 7.54) (See GSM sections 7.54 and 7.21)
In Kuali, the term program refers to all credential types; Degrees, majors, minors, and certificates. In the Manual, program refers to a graduate student’s major field of study.

A secondary concentration of undergraduate courses that provides students with a defined area of study outside their major. A minor generally requires 18 or more credits and is listed on the student’s permanent academic record after graduation.
University Manual 8.20.50 Minor Fields of Study. Undergraduate Students may declare a “minor” field of study. A minor is a secondary concentration of courses.

18 or more credits of related studies offered by one or more departments or programs and sponsored by a faculty member. (UM 8.20.50)
At least 12 credits at the 200-level or above ( UM 8.20.51)
At least 8 credits must be earned at URI (UM 8.20.51)
Minimum GPA average of 2.0 must be earned in the minor’s required courses (UM 8.20.51)
A maximum of two courses can apply to both the major and minor field of study (UM 8.20.52)
An approved course of study designed to further knowledge in a field of interest, provide specialized training, and/or enhance professional skills.

Undergraduate certificates generally require 15-21 credits of coursework (UM 8.20.70)
Undergraduate certificates are available to degree seeking and certificate-only seeking undergraduate students (UM 8.20.70)
Undergraduate certificate courses may not be pass/fail (UM 8.20.71)
Graduate certificates require 12 credits minimum, 16 credits maximum. (GSM Appendix J.1.1)
Post-master’s graduate certificates require 12 credits minimum, 18 credits maximum. (GSM Appendix J.1.1)

The curriculum approval process generally follows the sequence shown in the URI Curricular Approval Process Flowchart. Specific steps may vary by college, department, proposal type, and whether the proposal requires additional levels of review.
URI Curricular Approval Process Flowchart

Proposal Development Faculty use the forms in Kuali Curriculum Management to develop the proposal and work with other stakeholders as appropriate.
Department Review The proposal is reviewed through the appropriate departmental process.
College Curriculum Committee Review The College Curriculum Committee reviews the proposal.
College Dean Approval The College Dean approves the proposal for Faculty Senate review.
Faculty Senate Curriculum Committee Review The Curriculum & Standards Committee, the General Education Committee, or the Graduate Council reviews the proposal.
Faculty Senate Approval The Faculty Senate considers the curriculum committee's recommendation and votes.
University President Approval Any curricular item that is not a course must be reviewed and approved by the University President.
URI Board of Trustees Approval In addition to the University President’s approval, new Majors and Degrees are also reviewed by the Board of Trustees.
An approval round is the sequence of review and approval activities that culminates in a Faculty Senate meeting. Multiple approval rounds occur throughout the academic year, and rounds may overlap.

Approval rounds overlap throughout the academic year, beginning with College Curriculum Committee review and culminating in Faculty Senate approval. Expand each round to see how the approval steps align.
Rounds 3, 5, and 7 include last chances for certain types of curricular approvals.

S/U Only
Tags: courses
Short Description: A grading method in which student performance is recorded as S (Satisfactory) or U (Unsatisfactory) rather than a letter grade.
S/U Only

Certain courses do not lend themselves to precise grading. For these courses, only S (satisfactory) or U (unsatisfactory) is given to all students enrolled. S/U courses are labeled as such in the course descriptions in this catalog. S/U courses are not counted as courses taken under the Pass-Fail option.
D1 is the only General Education outcome that can be graded using S/U or Letter Grades. All other outcomes must be graded by Letter Grades.

From your browser, navigate to Kuali Curriculum Management (CM).
Select Curriculum to open your Dashboard .
Related toolkit entry: Dashboard
From the left-hand navigation menu, select Courses.
On the Courses page, use the search bar at the top to find the course you would like to modify. You can search by:
Course code (e.g., COM100)
Course title (e.g., Communication Fundamentals)
Keywords found in the course title, description, or anywhere in the course form.
Once you locate the course, select it to open the current version
With the current course open, select Propose Changes in the upper-right corner of the window.
A window will appear prompting you to select Create a new version or Create a new revision. Always select Create a new version.
The following sections of this walkthrough are grouped by section of the proposal form.

This is where you will indicate the changes you are proposing to make to the course.
Select the type(s) of change: Check Major, Minor, or both, depending on the changes you are proposing. If you’re not sure which category applies, that’s okay! Select an option to view the list of changes included in that category.
Select the specific change(s): From the list(s) that appear, check the box next to each Major and/or Minor change you are proposing.
